title: Locate a binary-nonrare near-mean atom in calibrated balanced classes
statement: Assume BAL-certified R and relative-interior target m with an exactly calibrated Gibbs law pi_theta. For phi(x)=sum log Gamma(x_i+1), trigamma<2 and local witness mu give 0<=E_mu phi-phi(m)<=dH_R^2. The Gibbs variational principle and H(pi_theta)<=sum[(m_i+1)log(m_i+1)-m_i log m_i]=O_R(1+L) imply E_pi phi-phi(m)<=O_R(1+L) and D_KL(mu||pi_theta)<=O_R(1+L). Therefore some actual x within H_R of m has pi_theta(x)>=2^-c_R_prime(1+L). This is an intrinsic local probability/entropy anchor, not a bound on all log-activity components or a resolution of outward-normal boundary accuracy.
